correctness.rationale: For any independent nonnegative weights, two-step rotational averaging yields a two-rate optimum by concavity. Bloch diagonalization gives the exact band minimum. The positive variables U,V satisfy UV=cos^2(pi/m); AM-GM with strictly positive prices uniquely solves the two-rate problem. A complex two-dimensional Fiedler vector has squared adjacent chord lengths proportional to the two price classes, giving a global Rayleigh upper bound for all independent weights. Equality forces its real and imaginary parts to remain eigenvectors, and noncollinear adjacent unit-circle chord pairs force every weight to match the candidate. m=2 is treated separately by a circular eigenvector with tunable phase. The stdlib exact verifier checked 48 rational cases and 1872 principal minors; finite tests supplement rather than replace the proof.

value.rationale: A natural cost-asymmetric ring diffusion problem receives an exact full-dimensional optimal design, unique positive rates and a closed-form spectral gap across all sizes. The exceptional C4 case equalizes rates despite unequal prices; for every longer even cycle the cheaper class receives strictly larger rates, and the asymptotic square-root cost ratio follows. Unlike a mere SDP formulation, this gives direct implementable cost-sensitive rate design and a sharp structural size boundary.
